The test image shows a tomato plant with one branch severely affected: dark brown/purplish-black stem, dried/withered leaves hanging dead, and what appears to be a light-colored lesion at the stem node junction. The rest of the plant looks green and healthy. This looks like a stem canker or wilt affecting a single lateral branch.

Top candidates: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Phytophthora_Blight. Let me view one reference from each.

Now I have all 8 views (plus one extra). Let me synthesize my findings.

**Test image key features:**
- Single lateral branch completely dead (dark brown/purplish-black stem)
- Leaves on that branch fully withered and dark
- Light yellow/white lesion visible at the node junction where the dead branch meets the healthy green main stem
- Rest of plant is healthy green

**Reference comparison:**
- **Alternaria Bugwood_4**: Dark/blackish stem canker with creamy-white lesion material at edges — matches the dark stem + white node lesion pattern well
- **Phytophthora Bugwood_21**: Dark collapsed stems, but affects multiple stems more broadly
- **Bacterial Canker Bugwood_1 & 4**: Yellowing/brown margin leaves, green stems — doesn't match dark stem color
- **Sclerotinia Bugwood_12**: Wilted stems, but different texture and pattern
- **Gray Mold Bugwood_13**: Fruit lesion, not matching

The single branch dieback with very dark/black stem discoloration and a light-colored canker lesion at the node junction is most consistent with Alternaria Black Molds Stem Cankers. The "black molds" description matches the dark stem, and canker girdling explains why only the branch above the node is dead while the main stem remains healthy.
